name: dungeon-ui-libs
description: Compact knowledge graph for AI agents working on dungeon-ui + the demo app. Pairs with the SQLite RAG index (db/rag.db). Read this FIRST to navigate; query RAG for chunk-level details.

patterns.signals: input() / model() / output() / signal() / computed() / effect()
patterns.global_layout_overrides_use_important: DgInputGroup + DgIconField mutate descendants' padding/border-radius across components with equal-specificity rules; !important is intentional and documented in those .scss files.
patterns.output_naming_avoid_native_collisions: NEVER name an output() after a native DOM event that the inner template fires (`change`, `input`, `focus`, `blur`, `click`, `submit`, `reset`, `select`). The native event bubbles from the inner element to the custom-component host, and Angular's `(eventName)` binding on the host becomes ambiguous — the @Output may silently fail to fire. Prefix or rename: `checkboxChange`, `inputEvent`, `focused`, `blurred`, `clicked`, `selectedChange`. PrimeNG follows the same convention (`onChange`, `onFocus`, `onBlur`).

style_budget.rationale: Default 4kB warning is too tight for rich layout components (calendar pickers, hierarchical menus, multi-field input-groups). 6kB matches the natural floor after optimization; 8kB error catches genuine bloat (e.g. DgButton.scss compiled to 8.6kB before its severity refactor).

style_optimization_recipes.severity_via_css_vars: DgButton.scss declares each severity as a block of CSS custom properties (--dg-btn-bg/fg/hover/soft); variant rules read them via var(...). Avoids @each loop generating N×M selector blocks.
style_optimization_recipes.shared_via_extend_placeholder: DgDatepicker.scss uses %dg-dp-btn-reset and %dg-dp-focus-ring placeholders with @extend so duplicated patterns merge into one comma-list selector at compile time.
style_optimization_recipes.single_rule_with_selector_list: DgInputGroup.scss writes 4 concerns (zero-radii, first/last-child outer corners, drop-left-border, lift-z-index) as one CSS rule each with hand-written 10–12-selector list — single declaration block instead of @each generating one rule per field.

vi_aliases.purpose: Vietnamese phrase → component name lookup. Use this BEFORE rag_query when the user's request is in Vietnamese — the embedding model may miss VN phrasing, but a literal lookup here resolves the component first, then the rag_query can use the English component name.

exports.name: DgButton
exports.purpose: Button — severity / variant / size / loading.

exports.name: DgInputText
exports.purpose: Text input with size/variant/invalid/fluid + ControlValueAccessor.

exports.name: DgInputMask
exports.purpose: Apply typing mask to any <input>; supports append-mode (default) and slot-mode (overwrite at click position).
exports.tokens: 9 = digit · a = letter · * = alphanumeric · others = literal separator

modes.append: auto-insert separators as user types from left
modes.slot: fill template (e.g. __/__/____); click into any slot to overwrite

exported_helpers.applyMask(rawInput, mask): Append-mode: drop chars that don't fit the next token; auto-insert literal separators.
exported_helpers.buildSlotTemplate(mask, slotChar): Slot-mode: build empty template (e.g. __/__/____) where each token slot holds slotChar.
exported_helpers.padToMask(value, mask, slotChar): Pad/extend a partial value with slot chars so it lines up with the mask shape.
exported_helpers.isAllSlots(value, mask, slotChar): True when every token position is still the slot char (treat as 'empty' for focusout).
exported_helpers.firstSlotPos(value, mask, slotChar): Index of the first slot-char position — caret target on focus.
exported_helpers.snapToToken(pos, mask): Snap a click cursor onto the next token position so click-to-edit lands on a slot, not a separator.
exported_helpers.insertString(value, text, start, end, ma: Slot-mode insert/overwrite at [start,end]; auto-skips literals; returns updated value + new caret.
exported_helpers.deleteBackward(value, start, end, mask,: Replace the token before the caret with slotChar (Backspace in slot mode).
exported_helpers.deleteForward(value, start, end, mask, s: Replace the token at the caret with slotChar (Delete in slot mode).

exports.name: DgInputNumber
exports.purpose: Numeric input with locale formatting (Intl.NumberFormat), spinner, min/max, currency/percent/decimal modes.

methods.increment(): Add `step` to the current value; clamp to `max`.
methods.decrement(): Subtract `step` from the current value; clamp to `min`.
methods.clear(event?): Reset value to null and emit `cleared`.

exports.name: DgInputGroup
exports.purpose: Layout wrapper that joins inputs + addons + buttons into one bordered group with flat shared edges; rounded corners only on first/last child.

exports.name: DgInputGroupAddon
exports.purpose: Static chip inside <dg-input-group> for icons / symbols / labels.

exports.name: DgIconField
exports.purpose: Overlay an icon INSIDE an input (left or right). Differs from input-group: no extra addon border; input gets internal padding for icon.

exports.name: DgInputIcon
exports.purpose: Single icon container inside <dg-icon-field>; absolutely positioned, vertically centered.

exports.name: DgDialog
exports.purpose: Modal/non-modal dialog built on native <dialog> + DgFocusTrap.

methods.close(): Set visible to false and emit `hidden`. (Inline-dialog API; programmatic dialogs close via DgDialogRef.close.)

exports.name: DgDialogService
exports.purpose: Programmatic dialog opener. open(component, config) → DgDialogRef.

methods.open<T,R,D,I>(component, config?): Instantiate `component` inside a host DgDialog, wire DG_DIALOG_DATA + setInput() inputs, return a DgDialogRef.

exports.name: DgDialogRef
exports.purpose: Handle returned by DgDialogService.open(); injected inside the dialog component for self-close + result reporting.

properties.componentInstance: The instantiated dialog content component (typed via generics).
properties.afterOpened$: Observable<void> — fires once after the dialog mounts.
properties.afterClosed$: Observable<TResult | undefined> — fires when close() is called (any source).

methods.close(result?): Close the dialog and resolve afterClosed$ with the optional result.
methods.afterClosed(): Promise wrapper around afterClosed$ for await-style flows.

exports.name: DgFocusTrap
exports.purpose: Confine Tab/Shift+Tab to focusable descendants. Inserts two visually-hidden sentinels that wrap focus.

methods.focusFirst(): Focus the first focusable descendant of the host (or the host itself if none).
methods.focusLast(): Focus the last focusable descendant of the host.

exports.name: DgCheckbox
exports.purpose: Click-to-toggle checkbox: binary mode (boolean / trueValue-falseValue) + multi (group) mode (array contributions), indeterminate state, custom icon template, label.

methods.toggle(originalEvent?): Programmatic toggle (respects disabled / readonly). Updates value via binary/multi rules and fires `checkboxChange`.

exports.naming_note: Output is `checkboxChange`, NOT `change` — `change` collides with the native DOM event bubbling from the inner <input>, making Angular's (change) binding on the custom-component host ambiguous / non-firing. Same reason PrimeNG's p-checkbox uses `onChange`.

exports.name: DgRadio
exports.purpose: Single-select radio. Group coordination via shared parent binding ([(value)] / [(ngModel)] / [formControl]) + DgRadioRegistry sibling-sync by `name`. Native `name` also drives browser-level Arrow-key nav.

methods.select(originalEvent?): Programmatically pick this radio (no-op when disabled / readonly / already checked). Updates `value` to `radioValue` and fires `radioChange`.

exports.naming_note: Output is `radioChange`, NOT `change` — same native-event collision rationale as DgCheckbox. Per-radio payload is `radioValue` (mirrors DgCheckbox's `checkboxValue`), distinct from PrimeNG's `value` to keep `value` for the model() group binding.
exports.registry_note: DgRadioRegistry (Injectable, providedIn: 'root') syncs sibling radios sharing the same `name` when one is picked. Required for [formControl] / [(ngModel)] groups: Angular's `setValue(v, { emitModelToViewChange: false })` from the originating accessor blocks `writeValue` propagation to OTHER directives bound to the same control, so siblings would keep stale `value` and all render checked. Mirrors PrimeNG's RadioControlRegistry. For [(value)] signal binding, sibling sync still works via the parent signal + Angular CD; the registry is idempotent there. **Always set `name` on radios in the same group** — without it, registry sync is a no-op.

exports.name: DgRadioRegistry
exports.purpose: Internal coordination service for DgRadio sibling-sync (see DgRadio.registry_note). Exposed for tests / advanced custom integrations; normal users never inject it directly.

methods.add(radio): Register a radio (called from DgRadio constructor).
methods.remove(radio): Unregister a radio (called via DestroyRef onDestroy).
methods.selected(picked): Sync siblings sharing `picked.name()`: each sibling's `value` is set to `picked.radioValue()` so its `checked` recomputes correctly.

exports.name: DgDropdown
exports.purpose: Custom-rendered select with filter, keyboard nav, body-portal, custom templates.

methods.toggle(): Open if closed, close if open (no-op when disabled).
methods.openPanel(): Force-open the panel and seed highlightedIndex with the selected (or first non-disabled) option.
methods.select(option, event?): Pick `option`: set value, emit selectedChange, close, restore focus to trigger.
methods.clear(event): Reset value to null and emit selectedChange(null).

exports.name: DgAutocomplete
exports.purpose: Single-select combobox with debounced (complete) event — parent owns suggestions; supports dropdown trigger, forceSelection, body-portal, custom item/empty templates.

methods.openPanel(): Open the suggestions panel; seed highlightedIndex with the first non-disabled option.
methods.select(option): Write `optionLabel` into the input, set value=optionValue, emit `selected`, close.
methods.clear(): Wipe input text + value, emit `cleared`, restore focus to the input.

exports.name: DgDatepicker
exports.purpose: Calendar / date picker — single or range, inline or popup, 3 views (date / month / year), button bar, week numbers, body portal.

methods.toggle(): Open if closed, close if open (no-op when disabled / inline).
methods.close(): Close panel; reset view back to 'date' so next open starts on the date grid.
methods.prev(): Step backwards by the current view's unit (month / year / decade).
methods.next(): Step forwards by the current view's unit (month / year / decade).
methods.setView(v): Switch view: 'date' | 'month' | 'year'. Emits monthChange/yearChange when relevant.
methods.selectMonth(month): From month view: pick `month`, return to date view at that month.
methods.selectYear(year): From year view: pick `year`, advance to month view of that year.
methods.prevMonth(): Move calendar one month earlier (date view).
methods.nextMonth(): Move calendar one month later (date view).
methods.goToday(): Jump the visible month to today; in single mode, also select today.
methods.clearAll(): Clear the bound value and close (no-op for inline).
methods.clear(event): Wrapper used by the × button; stops propagation then clears.

exports.name: DgNavMenu
exports.purpose: Hierarchical menubar / sidebar / tabs — PrimeNG-aligned MenuItem with command/url/items, mobile drawer, multi-level submenus.
exports.item_shape: MenuItem-aligned: label, icon, value (active key), command, url, target, routerLink, items, expanded, disabled, visible, escape, separator, badge, tooltip, id, tabindex, style, styleClass, iconClass, labelClass, linkClass, badgeStyleClass, data

methods.toggleMobile(event): Toggle the mobileActive drawer state (only meaningful below the breakpoint).

exports.name: DgTable
exports.purpose: Div-based virtual-scrolling table with client/server/cursor pagination, bottom-anchor sizing, slot-customizable paginator.

methods.scrollToIndex(index): Scroll the virtual viewport so the row at `index` is in view (clamped to data length).

exports.name: DgTableBottomAnchor
exports.purpose: Marker that DgTable observes (ResizeObserver) to fit its height to a given anchor's top position.

shell.layout: Grid: sidebar (16rem, scrolls independently) | main (overflow auto, scrollbar at viewport right edge).

prerender.mode: static (outputMode in angular.json) — every route in app.routes.ts is prerendered to its own index.html at build time. No runtime SSR server; output is static files servable by any CDN / static host.
entry_files: src/main.server.ts — bootstrap fn MUST forward BootstrapContext: `(ctx) => bootstrapApplication(App, config, ctx)`. Without forwarding ctx the build fails NG0401 'Missing Platform' during route extraction.
src/app/app.routes.server.ts — single `{ path: '**', renderMode: RenderMode.Prerender }` rule; the route extractor walks the client router config (app.routes.ts) and prerenders each match.
src/app/app.config.ts — provideClientHydration(withEventReplay()) so the prerendered HTML hydrates without flicker and queued events replay after JS loads.
prerender.output_layout: dist/dungeon-ui-libs/browser/<route>/index.html for each route + prerendered-routes.json manifest. index.csr.html is the client-side-render fallback shell.

search.purpose: Static curated search index (~50 entries). Filters by title + page + keywords; redirects to route. Keyboard nav (↑↓/Enter/Esc).

demo_dialogs.purpose: 3 example components opened via DgDialogService — used by /dialog page.

relationships.to: DgInputText | DgInputNumber | DgDropdown | DgDatepicker | DgButton | DgInputGroupAddon

relationships.via: absolute-positioned icon + reserved padding on field classes

primeng_alignment.rationale: dungeon-ui mirrors PrimeNG's component shape (input names, MenuItem, MenuItemCommandEvent) so users coming from PrimeNG learn the API in minutes — without bringing PrimeNG as a runtime dep.
primeng_alignment.primeng_ref_path: ../primeng-ref (sibling repo, ingested in RAG with project_id=primeng)

components_modelled_after.DgInputNumber: p-inputnumber (subset: no time picker / no advanced repeat)
components_modelled_after.DgAutocomplete: p-autoComplete (single-select subset: no multi-select chips, no virtual scroll, no group)
components_modelled_after.DgCheckbox: p-checkbox (binary + multi/group modes, indeterminate, custom-icon template; subset — no parent context provider, no autofocus, no inputStyle/Class)
components_modelled_after.DgRadio: p-radioButton (subset — single-select with shared signal/CVA binding + DgRadioRegistry sibling-sync by `name`; no autoFocus, no per-radio tabindex management)
components_modelled_after.DgDatepicker: p-datepicker (subset: no time picker / no multi-month / no touch UI)

DgCheckbox: ariaLabelledBy (use plain aria-labelledby attr if needed)
parent-aware group context provider (consumers manage the array via reactive forms / signals)
DgRadio: ariaLabelledBy (use plain aria-labelledby attr if needed)
general: form validators inside library (consumers wire validators externally)

rag.primeng_ref_layout: Each component lives at packages/primeng/src/<name>/ (e.g. autocomplete, datepicker, menubar). Spec files at packages/primeng/src/<name>/<name>.spec.ts.
rag.ingest_recipe: Use mcp__dungeon-rag__rag_ingest with explicit project_id when adding new sources. project_id='dungeon-ui' for our lib + docs; project_id='primeng' for ../primeng-ref/**.
rag.memory_rule: After any change under projects/dungeon-ui/src/lib/** or public-api.ts: (1) update docs/dungeon-ui-overview.md, (2) update knowledge-graph.json (library.exports + relevant patterns/skipped/alignment sections), (3) re-ingest lib path + docs/ into RAG with project_id='dungeon-ui'.
rag.primeng_explore_rule: When exploring a primeng component (to model a new dungeon-ui counterpart, or to compare API), ingest its folder with project_id='primeng' BEFORE deep-reading: mcp__dungeon-rag__rag_ingest path='../primeng-ref/packages/primeng/src/<name>'. Future agents can then RAG-query the same component without re-walking the FS.

primeng_indexed.purpose: Registry of primeng-ref folders already ingested into RAG. Check this BEFORE rag_query to avoid the miss-then-ingest-then-query round-trip; if the target is listed, query directly. Update this list whenever rag_ingest runs against ../primeng-ref.

model_orchestration.purpose: Cost / latency optimization. Route mechanical sub-tasks to the lightest model that can do the job; reserve heavier models for design + implementation. Parallelize independent sub-tasks via multiple tool calls in one message.

haiku.use_for: Single-shot lookups, status checks, JSON validation runs, simple ingest commands. Fastest + cheapest.

sonnet.use_for: Mechanical structured edits where the SHAPE is dictated by an existing template. Most subagent work falls here.
examples: write a showcase page using <closest-sibling>-page.ts as the template
append an entry to library.exports following the existing schema
add a route + nav item + search-index rows
append a docs section using the existing component-section template
rename a CSS class across files

opus.use_for: Steps where bad reasoning produces broken code (not just badly-formatted code). Design + implementation + non-trivial bug diagnosis. Cross-file reasoning.
examples: DESIGN scope-down (which p-X features map cleanly, which to deliberately_skip, edge cases)
IMPLEMENT a new dg-X by translating the p-X API to project conventions while preserving CVA / signal / OnPush patterns
DIAGNOSE a bug whose root cause spans multiple files or relies on Angular timing (effect, change detection, DI scope)

parallelization_groups.add_component_step_8: Showcase wiring splits into 4 independent edits — pages/<name>/<name>-page.ts, app.routes.ts, app.ts (nav model), search/search-index.ts. Spawn up to 4 parallel Agent calls (model=sonnet) in ONE message OR do them inline if the diff is small.
parallelization_groups.add_component_step_11: Two builds independent: `ng build dungeon-ui` (lib only) + `ng build` (showcase prod). Issue both Bash tool calls in ONE message.
parallelization_groups.add_component_step_12: Two ingests independent: rag_ingest projects/dungeon-ui/src + rag_ingest docs/. Call both MCP tools in ONE message.
parallelization_groups.fix_bug_step_4_5_6: When the fix is mechanical, build verification + graph update + re-ingest can fan out: Bash(ng build), Edit(graph.json), MCP(rag_ingest) — same message.
parallelization_groups.constraint: Never parallelize edits to the SAME file — Edit tool conflicts. Parallelize across DIFFERENT files only.

add_component.2_load_context: main (graph.json is already in context after step 1)
add_component.3_rag_query_lib: main OR delegate to haiku — single tool call either way
add_component.6_implement: opus — writes lib/<name>/<name>.ts following closest-sibling pattern; reads multiple files
add_component.7_export: sonnet — single targeted Edit on public-api.ts
add_component.9_docs: sonnet — append section to dungeon-ui-overview.md following template
add_component.10_update_graph: sonnet — append entry + alignment + skipped + route + (if applicable) primeng_indexed
add_component.12_re_ingest: main + 2 parallel MCP calls (lib path + docs path)

fix_bug.2_diagnose: opus — full file Read + cross-file reasoning
fix_bug.3_fix: opus if root cause is non-obvious; sonnet if the patch is mechanical (e.g. swap a CSS selector, fix a typo, retarget a regex)
fix_bug.5_update_graph: sonnet — only if API surface changed (input/output/method/scope-down)

principles: Default to Sonnet for delegated subagent work — handles ~80 % of mechanical tasks well and is significantly cheaper than Opus.

Reserve Opus for steps 5 + 6 (design + implementation) of add_component and step 2 (diagnose) of fix_bug. Bad reasoning at these steps produces broken code; saving cost on a wrong implementation isn't a win.
Parallelize aggressively across DIFFERENT files. Same-file edits must serialize.

When delegating, the subagent prompt must be SELF-CONTAINED: include the closest-sibling file path (from rag_query result), the scope-down list, links to the graph sections (vi_aliases / patterns / style_optimization_recipes) that the subagent should follow. Subagents start with no conversation context.

bootstrap.purpose: First-time / fresh-clone setup: wire RAG so every later workflow can rely on it. Run once per environment.
steps: 1. Verify the local llama.cpp servers are up: mcp__dungeon-rag__rag_status. Both URLs must respond and total_chunks must be readable. If status fails → start the embedding + LLM servers per the dungeon-rag MCP server README before continuing.
2. Ingest dungeon-ui source: mcp__dungeon-rag__rag_ingest path='projects/dungeon-ui/src' project_id='dungeon-ui'.
3. Ingest docs: mcp__dungeon-rag__rag_ingest path='docs' project_id='dungeon-ui'.
4. Ingest the showcase app (so demo-page patterns are searchable): mcp__dungeon-rag__rag_ingest path='src/app' project_id='dungeon-ui'.

5. Optional but recommended — bulk-ingest commonly-needed primeng components into project_id='primeng'. Use the patterns.primeng_indexed.components list as the seed set; subsequent add_component runs will extend it.
6. Run scripts/validate-graph.mjs (or npm run validate:graph) to confirm graph.json shape matches the filesystem. Fix any drift it reports BEFORE shipping changes built on top of stale info.

add_component.purpose: Standard flow for adding a new dungeon-ui component modelled after a PrimeNG counterpart. Optimized to minimize tokens via RAG instead of broad FS scans.
steps: 1. [main] CLARIFY input: confirm the user's component name + target PrimeNG model (default: same name, e.g. 'autocomplete' → p-autoComplete).

2. [main] LOAD context: read this knowledge-graph.json (already in context if you read it once) to see existing patterns, exports, primeng_alignment, deliberately_skipped, vi_aliases, primeng_indexed.

3. [haiku|main] RAG-query our lib: mcp__dungeon-rag__rag_query project_id='dungeon-ui' for the closest existing component. Surfaces patterns to copy: CVA, body-portal, panelWidth, optionLabel/Value getter, template directives, scss conventions.

4. [main] RAG-query primeng-ref: FIRST check rag.primeng_indexed.components — if the target name isn't there, run mcp__dungeon-rag__rag_ingest path='../primeng-ref/packages/primeng/src/<name>' project_id='primeng' AND append the name to primeng_indexed.components in this graph. THEN mcp__dungeon-rag__rag_query project_id='primeng' for the target component's API. Saves a query round-trip when the answer would have been empty.

5. [opus] DESIGN scope-down: list which PrimeNG features will be supported and which deliberately skipped; record under deliberately_skipped[ComponentName]. Reasoning-heavy — bad scope-down produces broken API.

6. [opus] IMPLEMENT: create lib/<name>/ with <name>.ts + <name>-defs.ts + <name>.scss + <name>.spec.ts + index.ts. Mirror style of the closest sibling. Use signals (input/model/output/signal/computed/effect), OnPush, booleanish for boolean inputs, ControlValueAccessor when value-bearing. Cross-file reasoning required.
7. [sonnet] EXPORT: add to projects/dungeon-ui/src/public-api.ts. Single Edit.

8. [sonnet × 4 parallel] SHOWCASE: pages/<name>/<name>-page.ts + app.routes.ts + app.ts nav + search/search-index.ts. Four DIFFERENT files — fan out. See model_orchestration.parallelization_groups.add_component_step_8.
9. [sonnet] DOCS: append a section to docs/dungeon-ui-overview.md following the existing component-section template (Inputs / Outputs / Templates / Behavior / Usage).

10. [sonnet] UPDATE this graph: add to library.exports, update demo_app.routes, primeng_alignment.components_modelled_after, deliberately_skipped, patterns.forms_cva / body_portal / vi_aliases / primeng_indexed if applicable.

11. [main + 2 parallel Bash] BUILD verify: ng build dungeon-ui (lib) AND ng build (showcase production) — issue both in one message. All component .scss must stay under the 8kB error budget. Then run npm run validate:graph.

12. [main + 2 parallel MCP] RE-INGEST: mcp__dungeon-rag__rag_ingest for projects/dungeon-ui/src AND docs/ (both project_id='dungeon-ui') in one message. Verify with rag_status (chunk count rises) + a confirmation rag_query.
forced_inputs_for_AI: Read knowledge-graph.json once at the start — every step below assumes it.
Use rag_query before broad FS scans — the index already covers our lib + docs + primeng-ref. Reserve grep/glob for after a focused RAG hit, not as the first move.
Copy patterns from the closest existing component, don't invent new conventions per component.

rag_query identifies the FILE, not the implementation. After a focused hit, ALWAYS Read the file (or the relevant range) for full context before editing — chunks are method-granular and miss surrounding declarations.

If the first rag_query returns mostly unrelated chunks (e.g. a CVA query lands on a NavMenu template-def), broaden top_k to 8–10 and add the file-class as a keyword (e.g. 'DgInputText input model writeValue') instead of falling back to grep.

Honor the [model: X] tag on each step — delegate via the Agent tool with that model. Spawn parallel Agent calls in ONE message when steps target different files (see model_orchestration.parallelization_groups). Steps tagged [main] stay on the orchestrator; steps tagged [haiku|sonnet|opus] route to that model.

fix_bug.purpose: Standard flow when the user reports a bug (visual glitch, runtime error, type error).
steps: 1. [main] LOCATE: rag_query project_id='dungeon-ui' for the symptom or the visible CSS class / public API name. Open the file at the returned path; only fall back to grep if RAG misses.

2. [opus] DIAGNOSE: read the file fully; confirm the failing logic. If the bug touches CSS, also re-read the SCSS — Angular Emulated encapsulation, !important conventions, component-style budgets all matter. Cross-file reasoning often needed.

3. [opus|sonnet] FIX: minimal change — don't refactor surrounding code. Use opus when root cause is non-obvious; sonnet when patch is mechanical (swap a CSS selector, fix a typo, retarget a regex). If the same anti-pattern exists in a sibling component, fix that too (one report → bulk fix), but only if the fix is mechanical.
4. [main + Bash] VERIFY: ng build dungeon-ui and (when CSS changed) ng build for the showcase, watching the SCSS budget warnings. Run npm run validate:graph if structure changed.

5. [sonnet] UPDATE knowledge-graph.json IF the fix changes a documented input/output, adds/removes a pattern, or invalidates an entry under deliberately_skipped. Skip the update for pure-visual fixes that don't change the API surface.
6. [main + parallel MCP] RE-INGEST when graph.json or any lib file changed: mcp__dungeon-rag__rag_ingest projects/dungeon-ui/src + docs/ (in one message).

navigation_hints_for_ai: FIRST move on any task: read this graph.json. SECOND move: rag_query (project_id='dungeon-ui' for our code, 'primeng' for upstream API reference). FS grep/glob is a fallback after a focused RAG hit — not the first move.
When asked about a component: locate by name in library.exports → read the listed path.
When asked 'where is X used': consult relationships array.
When generating new component: follow workflows.add_component step-by-step. Don't skip the rag_query of the closest sibling — that's where the patterns to copy live.

When fixing a bug: follow workflows.fix_bug. Re-ingest only if a lib file or graph.json changed; pure visual SCSS edits are still ingested (they're under projects/dungeon-ui/src), but graph.json doesn't always need an update for them.
When exploring a primeng component for the first time: ingest its folder via rag.primeng_explore_rule before deep-reading. Subsequent agents save tokens by RAG-querying instead of FS-scanning.

When the user describes a behavior in Vietnamese: FIRST consult patterns.vi_aliases to map the Vietnamese phrase to a Dg* component name, THEN rag_query with the English component name. Embedding models may miss VN phrasing; the alias table resolves it deterministically. Also fall back to src/app/search/search-index.ts (curated VN keywords for navigating to demo pages).
When uncertain about specificity / encapsulation issues: check input-group.scss header comment — it documents the equal-specificity gotcha and the !important convention.
When a component .scss exceeds 6kB compiled: see patterns.style_optimization_recipes for the three documented compression patterns before bumping the budget.

When delegating sub-tasks: see model_orchestration.workflow_step_models for which model handles each step. Default to Sonnet for mechanical edits; Opus for design + implementation; Haiku for simple lookups. Parallelize per model_orchestration.parallelization_groups.
